title: Configurable DSP-Based CAM Architecture for Data-Intensive Applications on FPGAs
problem: FPGA-based Content-Addressable Memory (CAM) implementations suffer from high LUT/BRAM resource utilization, limited scalability, and suboptimal performance due to inefficient parallel search operations.
motivation: CAMs are essential for networking, database indexing, and graph processing, but traditional FPGA-based CAM designs waste resources on control logic, preventing high-speed data-intensive applications.
method: A CAM (memory that retrieves data by searching its content rather than using an address) traditionally wastes FPGA resources by using LUTs (basic logic building blocks) and BRAM (dedicated memory blocks). This design repurposes DSP blocks—circuits originally built for signal processing—which have built-in storage and comparison logic. These blocks perform many parallel searches across stored values simultaneously and can process multiple search queries without slowing down, speeding up both search and update operations. You can configure the memory width, capacity, and degree of parallelism to match your application.
key_novelty: This design uses DSP blocks (circuits built for signal processing) as the primary resource instead of traditional FPGA memory blocks, which reduces search and update time and enables multiple simultaneous queries.
contributions: DSP-block-based CAM architecture replacing LUT/BRAM-centric designs
Configurable multi-query support with efficient parallelism
Enhanced operating frequency and improved performance vs. traditional designs
Demonstrated effectiveness on triangle counting graph application

metrics.other: Higher operating frequency, improved performance, reduced search/update latency

primary_theme: DSP-block-based configurable CAM for high-performance FPGA applications
